items.title: How fixed cost per user shrinks as your user base grows
items.description: The reply-suggestions feature reserves $3,200/month of GPU capacity regardless of headcount, plus $0.011 per suggestion generated. Drag the user count to see how spreading that same $3,200 over more or fewer users changes the blended cost per user (each user generating the free tier's average of 25 suggestions/month).
items.compute: const fixed = 3200; const variableRate = 0.011; const generationsPerUser = 25; const costPerUser = fixed / params.users + variableRate * generationsPerUser; return { costPerUser };

items.title: Capping free-tier usage shrinks the loss — but doesn't fix it
items.description: L3's checkpoint asks what happens if free-tier generations are capped instead of removed. Drag the monthly generation cap per free user to see the free tier's total monthly cost move — and notice it never reaches $0, because free-tier revenue is $0 regardless of usage, so the segment's ~$2,667 share of fixed cost is a loss at any cap.

params.name: generationCap
params.label: Generations allowed per free user / month

items.compute: const freeUsers = 40000; const totalUsers = 48000; const fixed = 3200; const variableRate = 0.011; const fixedShare = fixed * (freeUsers / totalUsers); const freeTierCost = fixedShare + variableRate * params.generationCap * freeUsers; return { freeTierCost };

items.title: Break-even: how many paid users does it take to cover the fixed cost?
items.description: Using the paid tier's price and per-user generation volume, this reproduces breakEvenUnits() from L3. Drag the monthly subscription price to see how a thinner or fatter contribution margin moves the break-even user count — at the default $12 price and 60 generations/user, this reproduces L3's own ~282-user break-even.
items.compute: const fixed = 3200; const variableRate = 0.011; const generationsPerUser = 60; const variableCostPerUser = variableRate * generationsPerUser; const margin = params.pricePerUser - variableCostPerUser; const breakEvenUsers = margin > 0 ? fixed / margin : null; return { breakEvenUsers: breakEvenUsers === null ? 999999 : Math.round(breakEvenUsers) };
